subject: POC access & success criteria — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — POC success criteria and next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Great to chat this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 2-week POC we discussed: 

Success criteria (what success looks like for Acme):
- Integration: Redwood API integrated with your ingestion pipeline; end-to-end inference on sample dataset (100k tokens/day).
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 512-token prompts on dedicated region-us model variant.
- Cost: steady-state per-token cost within your target range (we'll provide runbook to measure).
- Quality: NPS-style rubric: 80%+ of sampled predictions meet your labeled evaluation criteria in the attached evaluation sheet.

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (you), Rishi (sales) — provisioning, monitoring, billing check-ins, quick triage.
- Acme: Sara (product owner), Tom (engineering lead), IT: approve network and SSO.
- Dev (cc'd): will provision API keys and IP allowlist template, and send SSO invites.

Timeline & milestones:
- Day 0 (this week): access + IP allowlist + SSO invites
- Day 1-3: integration & smoke tests
- Day 4-10: run evaluation suite, collect quality metrics
- Day 11-14: review results + decision meeting

Next steps (action items):
1) Acme IT to whitelist the IP ranges Dev sends (see template).
2) Confirm the list of users for SSO invites (email addresses).
3) Dev will provision a scoped API key (valid for 14 days) and upload the evaluation spreadsheet.
4) Schedule a mid-POC sync (Day 7) — propose Tue Aug 10 11am PT.

I've attached an evaluation template and the POC requirements workbook for your team to fill in: [Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)].

If that all looks good please reply with the SSO invite list and IT contact for IP whitelisting so Dev can send the technical details.

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Tom / IT team —

Thanks — attaching the IP allowlist template (below) and the two outbound ranges we use for POCs in us-west: 

- 52.34.120.0/24
- 52.34.121.0/24

These are the public egress IPs for the dedicated POC pool. If you need CIDR aggregation for your firewall rules let me know and I can provide the exact NAT mappings.

SSO notes (Okta):
- We support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO. For this POC the simplest flow is an IdP-initiated SAML link or add the two users via a short invite flow. Required attributes: email, firstName, lastName.
- RBAC: we can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; for the POC we recommend a single group called "acme-poc-users" with read/write inference access.

API key provisioning (temporary):
- I'll create a scoped API key limited to the POC project and set a 14-day expiry. Key will be delivered via the secure link below. Key rotation: supported via the console and CLI.

Attachments: [Attachment: ip_allowlist_template.txt (text/plain)]
Links: https://docs.redwood.inference.com/onboarding/poc-runbook
Secure key delivery (will send after you confirm IP whitelist): https://app.redwood.inference.com/secure-keys/ACME-542

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through firewall config.

— Dev Patel
